LEARNING PATH LESSON · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Notice, Pause, Breathe & Reset — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson gives your family a single, blame-free power move: the RESET — four steps that stop a going-sideways moment and start it again, fresh, no guilt attached.

What is this?

Notice spots the moment tipping, pause stops everything mid-motion, breathe runs one slow breath through the group, and reset starts the bit again from the top — same game, fresh start, nobody in trouble.

What does it mean?

Most meltdowns spiral because nobody has a word that stops them without blame. RESET is that word: it names the moment, not the child — the play tipped, so we reset the play. Nobody is the villain of a reset.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three ideas: the noticing is a SKILL (spotting the wobble before the crash — the raised hand, the too-loud voice); the pause includes the grown-up (everyone freezes — that is the fun and the fairness); and reset means FRESH — the last thirty seconds are not brought to the new start as evidence.

Why this matters

This card is the emergency word for the whole family system: siblings’ games, parent-child standoffs, the pre-dinner spiral. One word, four steps, blame-free — the single highest-leverage habit in the class.

What it teaches

Early warning detection (noticing escalation before it lands), group co-regulation (the shared pause), fresh-start thinking (separating the moment from the child), and family culture — the rituals that make a household feel safe.

Words to learn

noticepausebreatheresetfresh startdo-overtogether

Say this to your child

“"Our family has a magic word: RESET. Here is how it works. Someone NOTICES — a hand goes up — uh oh, this is tipping over. Everyone PAUSEs — mid-motion, even grown-ups, even the dog if he will cooperate. One slow BREATHE together — in through the nose, out slow, the whole room settles an inch. And then: RESET — the game, the moment, the whole bit starts again from the top, fresh. Here is the rule that makes it magic: nobody is in trouble at a reset. Not you, not me. The moment just begins again. Watch me do it to myself sometime — grown-ups need the reset button most of all."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "The reset button — for moments going sideways."
  2. Read the panels: the hand-raised girl NOTICEs, the still boy PAUSEs, the folded-hands boy BREATHEs, the refreshed girl RESETs with a small fist.
  3. Play reset-tag below until the word itself does the work.
  4. Demo a grown-up reset: mid-fluster (spilled juice, lost keys), call RESET on yourself — hand up, freeze, one breath, "okay — fresh start." The self-reset is the strongest model in the house.
  5. Close with the takeaway: "nobody is in trouble at a reset — the moment just begins again."

Look closer at the picture

On this card four panels run the reset: Notice, an attentive girl with her hand raised; Pause, a still boy with closed eyes; Breathe, a boy with folded hands mid-breath; and Reset, a refreshed girl with a small fist up — the family’s emergency word, drawn calm.

Ask your child

"What does the raised hand mean?" "Who has to pause — just kids, or everyone?" "Is anyone in trouble at a reset?" "What gets to start again?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "RESET!" (hand up, delighted) "you have to pause TOO, Daddy" or the merciful one: "we reset, nobody is in trouble."

Out in the real world

Reset moments repeat daily: the game that turns shouty, the dinner-table wobbles, the getting-out-the-door chaos, the sibling spiral. The word works on everyone’s moments — and the day your child calls RESET on YOUR fluster, the habit is fully installed (it will happen; be ready to honour it instantly).

Try it together

Reset Tag: play any fast game — catch, tickle-monster, dance — with the family rule that anyone may shout RESET. When it is called: freeze, one breath together, then the game restarts from the top. The giggles come from the pausing mid-pounce (especially the grown-up caught mid-tickle). After a week of play-resets, the word starts working on real storms — same freeze, same breath, same fresh start, now with a purpose.

Understanding check

Ask: "Who can call reset? What happens to the last thirty seconds? Is anyone in trouble?" Anyone, left behind, nobody — three answers and the family has its button.

Parent tips

Honour every reset instantly — a reset that gets argued with ("we are NOT resetting, we are LEAVING") teaches the word is decoration. And keep the no-blame rule sacred: the moment anyone adds "this is your fault" to a reset, the magic dies. The fresh start IS the discipline; it needs nothing else attached.

This lesson pairs with the Notice, Pause, Breathe & Reset flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).
